clue.text: VIP can go over a judge's head

definitions.meaning: a very important person, a big shot

definitions.text: can go over a judge's head
definitions.meaning: a judge in court wears a large wig on top of the head

explanation.surface: An important person can leapfrog a judge and appeal to a higher authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over someone's head' suggests bypassing them; here it is literal, the headgear a British judge wears.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a person of importance; read literally, a large wig is worn by British judges.

clue.text: The little woman should be considered

parts.note: Beth March is one of the four sisters in Little Women
ought means should

explanation.surface: The wife ought to be taken into account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The little woman' sounds like an old phrase for a wife; it is Beth from Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of bethink, to reflect or call to mind.

clue.text: Sharing out the embellishment

indicators.note: letters put out of order are rearranged

explanation.surface: Handing round the decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SHARING.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration for food on a plate, or any ornament.

clue.text: Scotsman with key taken in by one pressing shopkeeper

indicators.note: says the Scotsman and key sit inside the person pressing clothes

parts.note: an ironer presses clothes
mon is the Scots form of man
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A Scot carrying a key is deceived by a pushy shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being deceived, and 'pressing' suggests pushy; here they mean placed inside, and ironing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardware dealer selling tools and metal goods.

clue.text: A measure of help in medication

definitions.text: A measure of help in medication

parts.words: A measure of help in medication
parts.note: recalls the Mary Poppins song in which a little sugar helps the medicine go down, measured with a kitchen implement

explanation.surface: A dose of assistance given along with medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of quantity taken with a household utensil, the amount that sweetens a dose in the famous song.

clue.text: As obstinate as Napoleon (Orwell)

parts.note: in Orwell's Animal Farm Napoleon is the pig at the head of the farm, so stubbornness is read as being led by a swine

explanation.surface: As stubborn as the dictator in Orwell's fable.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon suggests the French emperor; it is the boar who rules Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn, and literally led by a swine as Animal Farm was.

clue.text: Pray leave 29 in pieces:

indicators.note: the letters of the first word depart from the answer to 29

parts.note: the answer to 29 across, depicts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Begging the pieces to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes P, R, A, Y in order from the answer to 29 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps of food left over from a meal.

clue.text: Some distance, of course

definitions.meaning: the mown strip on a golf course

explanation.surface: Quite a way, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally'; it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair long way; also the closely mown part of a golf links.

clue.text: Like the crane-fly, lay not a round egg

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the egg
the A is excluded from the word lay

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to the crane-fly: don't lay a round egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes A from LAY to leave LY, and 'round' puts LY around EGG. The crane-fly is the long-legged insect called daddy-long-legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-limbed, as the daddy-long-legs insect famously is.

clue.text: People always have an excuse

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: People always make excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in peoPLE Always.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is a pleading or justification offered.

clue.text: Time, they say, to reduce friction and trouble

indicators.note: signals that the word for time is heard rather than spelt, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as in a school term
oil is applied to lubricate moving parts

explanation.surface: Advice that, as people say, it's time to ease the friction and the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' makes TERM a sound only: it is spelt TURM in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe confusion, upheaval and disorder.

clue.text: The modest minimum. one needed to fiddle

definitions.meaning: the scantiest garment that preserves modesty
a fiddle (violin) needs its lowest string, tuned to G

explanation.surface: The least a person can get away with, one needed to cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests cheating, but it is the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny garment covering only the essentials, and also a violin's lowest string.

clue.text: A confessed drug addict

parts.note: alludes to Thomas De Quincey's book Confessions of an English user of laudanum and the poppy drug

explanation.surface: Someone who admits to a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confessed' points to De Quincey's 1821 memoir, whose title names this kind of addict.
explanation.definitionFit: De Quincey's memoir describes his addiction to a poppy-derived narcotic, taken by mouth.

clue.text: A Sussex town pronounced wrongly

indicators.note: tells the solver the town's name is to be heard and spelt as a different word of the same sound

parts.note: Rye is a small historic town in East Sussex, England

explanation.surface: Someone mispronounces the name of a town in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: RYE is an old town in East Sussex; 'pronounced' turns it into WRY, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew or off course, as when plans go amiss.

clue.text: Flowers, to plant round the Museum

parts.note: blooms are flowers
to bury is to put in the ground

explanation.surface: Flowers to be planted around the museum garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The London district around the British Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of central London that surrounds the British Museum.

clue.text: Hell for example turning red.

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for 'for example' is read backwards

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia
henna is a reddish-brown dye

explanation.surface: Hell, say, turns red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses EG to give GE. 'red' looks like a colour adjective but is henna, the reddish dye.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical valley of fire used as a name for the place of damnation.

clue.text: Shy member of the family

definitions.meaning: a shy is a target for throwing at, as at a fair
an aunt with the name Sally

explanation.surface: A bashful relative.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a British fairground game where balls are thrown at a dummy figure; 'Shy' means a throw, not timid.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground target to throw at, and literally a relative called Sally.

clue.text: Late bet indeed!

annotationWithheld.why: Late bet indeed! (7): wordplay is LAY (bet) in DEED, so 'indeed' is both the container indicator 'in' and the fodder DEED, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: American boy's caught' by debt-collectors in Kent

indicators.note: the boy's name is held inside the word for debt-collectors

parts.note: duns are people who demand payment of debts
Gene is an American boy's name; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An American lad is caught by bailiffs in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a shingle headland in Kent, England; 'in Kent' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland on the coast of the English county, known for its shingle and power station.

clue.text: Bring up holding of foreign. exchange

indicators.note: the word for rearing a child grips a foreign word inside it

parts.note: to train a child is to bring it up
de is French for 'of'

explanation.surface: Raising one's holdings of foreign currency on the exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign exchange' reads as one phrase but splits: 'of foreign' is French DE, and 'exchange' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing in an old item as part payment for a new one is a form of swap.

clue.text: Pity scholar accepts thanks by way of return. (he can't expect money)

indicators.note: all the pieces are read backwards
the scholar takes on the thanks, so the word for thanks stands beside the scholar's letters

parts.note: rue means pity or regret
ta is British slang for thanks
MA, Master of Arts, a scholar

explanation.surface: A pitiable scholar takes thanks in return, expecting no pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' sets TA beside MA, and 'by way of return' reads RUE, TA and MA backwards as one run, giving the answer. 'Pity' looks like an exclamation but is RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional does it for love, not pay.

clue.text: The same sort of Roman janitor

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same

indicators.note: suggests a loose version of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Roman caretaker of much the same kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The same' looks like a phrase about sameness; it is DO, short for ditto. 'sort of' makes ORMAN from ROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter who keeps the entrance of a building.

clue.text: Hood's summer time in Rome perhaps

indicators.note: the time abbreviation is placed inside
the city name may be rearranged

parts.note: BST is British Summer Time

explanation.surface: Robin Hood takes a summer break in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ROME to MOER, with BST (British Summer Time) 'in' it; a hood is a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a gangster or thug.

clue.text: Ring the changes on 9 bells

indicators.note: to ring the changes is to vary something, so the letters of the answer to 9 are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 9 down, an excuse

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers working through changes on nine bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring the changes on' looks like bell-ringing but rearranges the answer to 9 down (an excuse).
explanation.definitionFit: A set of tuned bells in a church tower.

clue.text: Drop round

explanation.surface: Drop in for a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: flop down heavily, and well-rounded or chubby.

clue.text: Apparent when large numbers have sacred book unopened

parts.note: OS means outsize, a clothing size
tens are numbers

indicators.note: the holy book loses its first letter

parts.note: the Bible is the Christian scripture

explanation.surface: It's clear when lots of figures accompany a holy book left closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes the first letter from BIBLE, leaving IBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeming or professed on the face of it, though perhaps not real.

clue.text: The end of the quarter

parts.note: a quarter is one of the four compass points, and London has a district called the End named after this quarter

explanation.surface: The close of a three-month period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' suggests three months; it is a compass quarter, and London's working-class district bears its name plus 'End'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of four cardinal compass points, the direction of sunrise.

clue.text: One employing improper ruse

indicators.note: an improper arrangement scrambles the letters

explanation.surface: Someone using a shady trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes use of something.

clue.text: Vessel is smashed in — let us.

indicators.note: breaking the words to pieces scrambles their letters

explanation.surface: A ship is wrecked: let us in!
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' rearranges IN and LETUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen container or pot is a household implement.

clue.text: …hurry and sink

definitions.meaning: to run with short quick steps
to sink a ship deliberately by holing it

explanation.surface: Run off and scupper the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: scamper away, or deliberately founder a vessel.

clue.text: Depicts harbour lights

parts.note: a port is a harbour
rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Paints the lights of the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shows or represents in a picture or performance.

clue.text: Sounds like the tree scene in Othello

indicators.note: tells the solver the name of the tree is heard, not spelt

parts.note: the cypress is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A tree seems to be the setting in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy moves from Venice to this Mediterranean island for most of its acts.
